content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposes to tackle the problem of continual self-supervised learning (where the self-supervised learning is applied on the data stream, which contains the data of different classes/tasks sequentially arriving) and particularly focus on addressing the issue of catastrophic forgetting without overfitting on the exemplars of previous classes/tasks stored in the replay buffer (named as rehearsal samples in this paper). The proposed method starts from the idea of selecting the most representative and discriminative samples from seen data (related to the ones which are closer to the corresponding class centers or the boundaries between classes) as the exemplars to be stored in the replay buffer, and due to the unsupervised setting (i.e. there is no label annotations for data samples), the authors introduce the "augmentation stability (denoted as AS, which is stemmed from the contrastive learning idea to construct a discriminator for estimating how likely a pair of augmented features encoded by the self-supervised model is from the same original image)", thanks to its positive correlation with the relative position of each sample in the corresponding class distribution, as a metric to evaluate the representativeness as well as discriminativeness of data samples. The strategy of selecting rehearsal samples based on the augmentation stability is then named as Augmentation Stability Rehearsal (ASR) in this paper. Based on the reply buffer updated by using the proposed ASR, the authors further introduce the framework "Contrastive Continuity on Augmentation Stability Rehearsal" stemmed on the concept of information bottleneck and contrastive learning to simultaneously preserve as much information shared among seen tasks/classes as possible for alleviating catastrophic forgetting and dismiss the redundant information for learning new knowledge. The proposed method is experimentally shown to achieve better performance in comparison to various supervised continual learning and continual self-supervised learning baselines.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
+ The overall organization is clear and the writing is easy to follow.
+ The idea of estimating the relative position of a sample in corresponding distribution via "augmentation stability" seems to be novel, and the proposed "Contrastive Continuity on Augmentation Stability Rehearsal" framework has also certain novelty to resolve the catastrophic forgetting issue without overfitting to the rehearsal samples. 
+ The efficacy of the proposed method is well demonstrated in the experiments to provide superior performance with respect to both supervised continual learning and continual self-supervised learning baselines. 

Weaknesses:
- There are some concerns regarding the method description and designs: 1) As described in the ASR update strategy, the rehearsal samples for previous tasks are based on the samples with high and low AS scores (the samples with middle AS scores are discarded) while for the current task the rehearsal samples are uniformly sampled from the corresponding data stream sorted by AS scores. Such difference between previous tasks and current task should be experimentally verified (for instance, why can't the current task follow the same principle as the previous tasks to select the rehearsal samples); 2) In line 5 of Algo.1, should it be noted that B^i_{t-}1 is already sorted according to the AS? 
- There are other concerns regarding the experimental settings and results: 1) As mentioned in Sec. 4.2, the mixup technique in LUMP is also adopted for the proposed method in the experiments on SplitCIFAR-100 and SplitTiny-ImageNet, there should be experimental results of excluding such mixup technique from the proposed method in order to demonstrate its pure contribution; 2) In order to better demonstrate the contribution of using ASR to update the reply buffer and its generalizabilty, there should be experiments of replacing the rehearsal buffer update strategy in the related works (for both supervised continual learning and continual self-supervised learning baselines that also adopt rehearsal buffer) by the proposed ASR update strategy.
- The idea behind "augmentation stability of each sample is positively correlated with its relative position in corresponding category distribution" is not well proven or verified. Though Fig.1 tries to serve such purpose to show such idea, but it is not enough, can the authors provide more solid discussion or even theoretical proof for such idea if it is possible? Moreover, currently there is a hidden assumption that the distribution of each category is single mode, but how if the category distribution is multi-modal (in which it is very likely to happen in more complicated datasets), will AS still be effective as a proxy to the relative positive in a category distribution?
- From my own research experience, for supervised continual learning, different strategies of rehearsal example selection (e.g. random or uniform) do not contribute significant difference to the final performance, can authors provide more discussion on the impact of particularly having both representative and discriminative rehearsal samples to the overall performance?
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: Overall, the clarity of the paper is satisfactory (well organization and good paper writing) and the proposed framework based on "Augmentation Stability Rehearsal" and  "Contrastive Continuity on Augmentation Stability Rehearsal" seems to be novel. However, there exists concerns on model design/description, experimental settings/results, as well as the solid discussion for "augmentation stability" which the authors should also address in order to further improve the overall quality.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall the proposed method for tackling the continual self-supervised learning problem seems to be novel and effective, but there are still some issues regarding the model design/description, experimental settings/results, and the idea behind "augmentation stability" that the authors should carefully address during the rebuttal. I would rate this paper marginally above the acceptance threshold according to its current status.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper presents a new method for Continual Self-supervised Learning (CSSL), a specific topic in the field of continual learning. In particular, the authors propose Augmentation Stability Rehearsal (ASR) to select representative examples to be saved in the rehearsal buffer to construct more informative buffer. The authors also propose Contrastive Continuity on Augmentation Stability Rehearsal (C2ASR) to balance forgetting and learning capacity. Comprehensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of the method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
- The high level idea of the paper is easy to capture.
- Discussion on Information Bottleneck (IB) with continual learning is interesting.

Main Weaknesses:
- The technical contribution of the paper is somewhat incremental, given existing prior work [1].
- The overall flow of the paper is a bit hard to catch. Specifically, there is no problem formulation of CSSL, which makes the paper not self-contained. One need to go back to [1] to have a clearer understanding of CSSL.
- As for the ASR, the high level intuition is to rank the data by some importance score to determine their priority to be buffered. I wonder how it performs comparing against some representative buffer selection methods, such as GSS [2], LARS[3], or DDR [4].
- For C2ASR, it seems quite heuristic. I wonder why it requires all previous snapshots, i.e. 1 to t-1. Is it possible to use only the current model (t) and the previous one (t-1)? Moreover, is the similarity measure important? Since you are inspired by the information bottleneck, is it possible to replace cosine similarity by mutual information-related loses?
- The analysis in the Experiments section lacks insights. I can see multiple sentences just to enumerate numbers, which are unnecessary.
- I cannot find an ablation study table to demonstrate the independent influence of each component, which ultimately makes the empirical evaluation not that strong.

Minor Weaknesses:
- In formulas, it would be clearer to use \operatorname{} to denote operations like "max" and "sim".
- Several typos.


[1] Fini, Enrico, et al. "Self-supervised models are continual learners." CVPR 2022.

[2] Aljundi, Rahaf, et al. "Gradient based sample selection for online continual learning."NeurIPS 2019.

[3] Buzzega, Pietro, et al. "Rethinking experience replay: a bag of tricks for continual learning." ICPR 2021.

[4] Wang, Zifeng, et al. "SparCL: Sparse Continual Learning on the Edge." NeurIPS 2022.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
The overall quality of the paper needs improvement to reach the quality of an ICLR paper.
The clarity of the work needs improvement.
The work is original, but the idea itself seems incremental.
content.summary_of_the_review: The motivation of the paper is good, since Continual Self-supervised Learning is an interesting topic and training large-scale self-supervised models in a continual fashion in practical in real-world applications. However, the idea of the paper is somewhat incremental and heuristic. Both the writing and empirical results need further improvement. Therefore, I think the paper requires a major revision before getting accepted to top conferences like ICLR.

content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper focuses on addressing the catastrophic forgetting in Continual Self-Supervised Learning (CSSL). Specifically, an Augmentation Stability Rehearsal (ASR) strategy is devised to store the most representative and discriminative samples for rehearsal, which helps to overcome the overfitting on the rehearsal samples. Secondly, based on ASR, a Contrastive Continuity on Augmentation Stability Rehearsal (C2ASR) method is proposed for CSSL to preserve the information shared among seen task streams and dismiss the redundant information in previous states. Experiments are conducted on several benchmarks to evaluate the proposed method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths:
+ Augmentation Stability Rehearsal (ASR) is devised to store the most representative and discriminative samples for rehearsal.
+ Based on ASR, a Contrastive Continuity on Augmentation Stability Rehearsal (C2ASR) method is proposed for CSSL.
+ The proposed method is evaluated on several popular CSSL benchmarks.

Weaknesses: 
- My major concern is on the insufficient ablation study of the proposed method. Since the proposed method consists of several key components, it is easy to conduct a detailed study by ablating a component each time. Meanwhile, both ASR and C2ASR can be easily modified when different strategies are used, and thus the comparison to these modified versions is needed. 
- The selection of the hyperparameters of the proposed method must be studied properly. This could help to reveal the significance of each key component of the proposed method.
- In Tables 1-2, the performance of the proposed method seems not that good on CIFAR-10. Please give a detailed discussion.

content.summary_of_the_paper: In this paper, the authors proposed a method that makes Self-supervised learning methods continually learn. To address the catastrophic forgetting problem, the proposed method uses the rehearsal technique, and the samples are selected based on the stability of the augmented samples. The authors compare the proposed methods with many state-of-the-art methods, showing remarkable improvements.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strength:
1. The research problem is important for the development of Self-supervised learning.

2. Looking for the typical samples in unsupervised learning is hard. The authors give a criterion based on the stability of the augmented samples.


Weakness:
1. The authors should give more explanation about why chooses the stability of augmented samples. Only section 4.5 is not convincing. For example, in uncalibrated datasets, some samples are out of domain, their augmentations can be also stable but they are not representative.

2. The stability of all examples will increase when the training process goes on.  So, I doubt does the method work for a long trained model (over 1000 epochs)? I think it is very important for lifelong learning.

2. The writing of this paper should be improved. The proposed selection criteria should be emphasized in the contribution part. The differences between the proposed method and SOTA methods should be discussed in related work. Algorithm 1 is hard to follow, and some notations are missing. Equation 6, 7, 8 add more complex notations but give little information.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
For clarity, the writing of the paper should be enhanced. Some parts are not easily understood. See weakness 3.

The overall quality of this paper is qualified. The sample selection criteria have some novelty. 

The authors give plenty of experiments. I think this work should be reproduceable.
content.summary_of_the_review: I think this is a qualified work although the writing should be improved. So, I recommend this work.

content.title: Contrastive Continuity on Augmentation Stability Rehearsal for Continual Self-Supervised Learning
content.TL;DR: This paper proposes C$^2$ ASR to address catastrophic forgetting in continual self-supervised learning
content.abstract: Self-supervised learning has attracted a lot of attention recently, which is able to learn powerful representations without any manual annotations. In order to cope with a variety of real-world scenarios, it also needs to develop the ability to continuously learn, i.e. Continual Self-Supervised Learning (CSSL). However, simple rehearsal or regularization will bring some negative effects while alleviating catastrophic forgetting in CSSL, e.g. overfitting on the rehearsal samples or hindering from learning fresh knowledge. In order to address catastrophic forgetting without overfitting on the rehearsal samples, we propose Augmentation Stability Rehearsal (ASR) in this paper, which selects the most representative and discriminative samples by estimating the augmentation stability for rehearsal. Meanwhile, we design a matching strategy for ASR to dynamically update the rehearsal buffer. In addition, we further propose Contrastive Continuity on Augmentation Stability Rehearsal (C$^2$ ASR) based on ASR, which preserves as much information shared among seen task streams as possible to prevent catastrophic forgetting and dismisses the redundant information to free up the ability to learn fresh knowledge. Our method obtains a great achievement compared with state-of-the-art CSSL methods on a variety of CSSL benchmarks. The source code will be released soon.
